skill.name: state-machine
skill.description: Renders every state of a component you choose on a throwaway page, with mock data and a switcher, so you can work on each state.
skill.summary: Build a temporary component workbench with realistic fixtures, grouped states, and shareable state URLs.
skill.author: jakubkrehel

content.user_title: Explore Component States with Realistic Fixtures
content.value_statement: Loading, error, and permission states can be difficult to reproduce during UI development. This skill builds a temporary component workbench with realistic fixtures and a grouped state switcher.
actual_capabilities: Identify reachable data, account, and feature states by reading the component and its data hooks.
Build a temporary route that imports the real component and inherits the application layout and providers.
Supply realistic fixtures through props, seeded query caches, mock providers, or existing request mocks.
Specify a grouped state switcher with URL selection, keyboard navigation, accessible labels, and a responsive select.
Check each state in an available browser and report when browser verification is unavailable.
Remove the temporary setup on user request and search for remaining route and fixture references.
limitations: Each run covers one component, not a complete page containing several independent components.
Only states supported by existing code are included; missing branches are listed rather than implemented.
Fixture injection may require an approved component change when no suitable data boundary exists.
Browser verification requires an available browser; the workbench does not replace automated test coverage.

use_cases.title: Inspect Data States
use_cases.description: Build a workbench for a table with loading, empty, error, and populated states using realistic row counts.

use_cases.title: Refine Permission Views
use_cases.description: Compare existing role and plan states in the real component without changing application styles or recreating the component.

use_cases.title: Reproduce Visual Regressions
use_cases.description: Use state URLs to revisit fixtures and check every state after a visual change.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Workbench
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the state-machine skill for [component]. Find its existing states and build a temporary page with realistic fixtures and a state switcher.

prompt_templates.title: Cover Data Variations
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a workbench for [component] covering reachable loading, empty, error, typical, and long-list states. Keep loading pending until I switch states.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Access Combinations
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [component] for role, plan, and feature branches. Group reachable states using product terms. Include combinations only where existing code branches on them.

prompt_templates.title: Isolate Complex Data Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a workbench for [component] using existing query caches or request mocks. Prevent live refetches from replacing fixtures. Verify each state and request approval before component edits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: isolate fixtures in an application with shared data providers.

output_examples.input: Create a state workbench for an audit log table with existing loading, empty, error, and populated branches.
output: Created a temporary page importing the existing audit log table at its production width.
Data states: Loading, Empty, Error, Typical Activity, and Long History.
Loading remains pending until another state is selected.
Each state has a URL using the __state parameter.
The workbench remains available until you request removal.

output_examples.input: Inspect the existing owner and member states of a billing card when no browser is available.
output: Missing design state: Trial Expired. No corresponding branch exists, so it was excluded.
Fixtures use the existing provider without editing the billing card.
Browser verification was unavailable. Open the supplied workbench URL to check each state.

best_practices: List reachable states before building and name groups using the product vocabulary.
Use realistic synthetic fixtures at the component data boundary and confirm that live data does not replace them.
Recheck every state after visual changes and request cleanup only when the workbench is no longer needed.
anti_patterns: Rebuilding a lookalike component or changing production branches solely to display invented states.
Using generic placeholder rows or allowing loading fixtures to resolve automatically.
Changing component visuals without a request or deleting the workbench before the user approves removal.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as compatible?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The workflow needs access to the application source.

faq.question: Does this provide a state machine runtime?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions for building a temporary UI workbench, not a runtime library or formal state machine engine.

faq.question: Does it edit the original component?
faq.answer: It imports the existing component unchanged. If fixture injection requires a new data boundary, it asks before making that change.

faq.question: How are states selected?
faq.answer: A grouped list controls the __state URL parameter. A select replaces the list when space is limited, and arrow keys navigate states.

faq.question: What happens when browser verification is unavailable?
faq.answer: The assistant reports that limitation and provides the workbench URL for the user to check.

faq.question: When is the temporary page removed?
faq.answer: Only after the user requests removal. Cleanup deletes the temporary setup and checks for remaining route and fixture references.
